transcript:
Header: 2026-08-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: 57m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Allen (NovaPayments Lead ML), Lea Torres (Head of AI), Tom Wu (SRE), Sana Riaz (Product), Eliot Park (Data)

[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, can we do quick roll call?
[00:07] Lea Torres: Lea here, sorry slight audio lag on my end.
[00:10] Marcus Allen: Marcus present.
[00:12] Tom Wu: Tom here.
[00:15] Jordan Kim: great, quick agenda: model pins, routing, and then the emergency cutover plan that Priya prepped. any additions?
[00:22] Sana Riaz: add the question about data residency and KMS — legal asked for clarity.
[00:26] Jordan Kim: good call, we'll cover that in the security block.

-- Summary of current pilot metrics --
[00:30] Priya Desai: we ran the last 72 hour run on the dedicated pool with the two candidate models — rwd-7b-q4f and rwd-13b-8k — results are in the shared sheet, quick takeaways: 7b with q4f has ~18% lower cost per token but 95th p99 latency for long seqs drifts up compared to 13b. prefix hit helps reduce tokens ~12% for the sample trace.
[01:01] Marcus Allen: that matches what we saw in prod-ish tests, but our retry patterns amplify tail latency; so p99 matters more to us than average.
[01:12] Priya Desai: understood, that's why we suggested a tiered routing policy — route time-sensitive queries to the 13b-8k variant and bulk/background to 7b-q4f.
[01:26] Tom Wu: question — can that routing be per-route or per-API key? we'd prefer per-service route because payments flow needs deterministic behaviour.
[01:35] Priya Desai: yes, you can pin at route level or set per-api-key as well; the runtime supports policy matching by route tags. it's in the console routing rules.
[01:46] Marcus Allen: in a failover, do you automatically fallback to hosted if dedicated is down? we don't want noisy region-to-region fallbacks causing invoice surprises.
[01:56] Jordan Kim: fallback behavior is policy-driven: you can choose model-variant fallback within dedicated, then region fallback, then hosted as last resort. and we can set cost caps + alerts so no silent spiky billing.

-- Cutover / emergency plan discussion --
[02:15] Priya Desai: ok, so the cutover runbook we walked through has three phases: detection -> isolation -> switch. detection via health probes (latency/error thresholds), isolation by draining traffic from failing nodes/model, switch via model pin flip and updated routing with a short-lived shadow to validate. recommended order is soft-fallback (shadow) then hard-cut after 30s stable.
[02:45] Marcus Allen: one worry is session state / KV cache while switching models — will we lose KV cache across variants? our fine-tuned convo state assumes same KV layout.
[02:57] Priya Desai: good question; if models are architecture-compatible and share the same kv-keyspace, the runtime will reuse the KV cache; otherwise we recommend a cache warmup policy and a brief grace period. also we support prefix-based cached responses to avoid full recompute for identical prompts.
[03:20] Eliot Park: can we snapshot the KV cache as part of the dry-run? like a read-only dump to validate warmup efficacy?
[03:28] Priya Desai: yes, we can export cache metrics and hit-rate, but not raw token contents for privacy reasons. you get hit percentages, keys counts, warmup times.

[03:40] Jordan Kim: Tom, from a networking perspective — any constraints for region failover?
[03:45] Tom Wu: we have strict egress whitelists and peering rules. if regions change IP blocks we need a plan for quick re-allowing. also we have an internal policy that mandates no cross-border data copies without approval.
[03:58] Jordan Kim: noted, that affects whether hosted region fallback is allowed — we'll mark hosted as a last-resort only and keep it off in the policy by default.

-- Security/compliance brief --
[04:10] Jordan Kim: quick update on docs: SOC2 report, ISO attestation and KMS integration guide are in the shared folder. Jordan to send explicit KMS flow for NovaPayments.
[04:21] Lea Torres: our legal will want an HSM diagram and proof of no plaintext storage in logs.
[04:26] Jordan Kim: yes, the runtime only stores encrypted model keys and audit logs are configurable to redact content. we'll include the architecture diagram.

-- Technical deep questions / dirty edges --
[04:40] Marcus Allen: if we pin model with a version tag, what's the rollback time to previous version in a canary rollback?
[04:46] Priya Desai: with pinned versions you can do instant routing flips; the canary window is configurable, but practically we see <30s for traffic switch if both versions are warmed. rollback is same path reversed. if the KV cache isn't compatible, warmup can add 10-90s depending on cache size.
[05:05] Marcus Allen: do you have a small script to do atomic pin flips via the API? we don't want to use console during incident.
[05:11] Priya Desai: yes, we can share API curl examples; Jordan will include a runbook snippet for atomic pin APICall.

[05:20] Tom Wu: what's the observability during cutover? token level traces? We need per-token timing for dispute investigations.
[05:28] Priya Desai: you get per-request and per-token aggregated metrics with trace IDs, and we can push traces into your Datadog or OpenTelemetry collector. raw token strings are not exported by default.

[05:42] Sana Riaz: on the routing tiers — is cost-based routing reactive (real-time price signals) or static config?
[05:50] Jordan Kim: today it's static config with autoscaling knobs; we have a cost-aware suggestion engine (Optimize) that recommends policies but we don't auto-swap models purely on price without a human flag.

-- Live review of the catalog sheet --
[06:05] Priya Desai: walking through the catalog, column A is model name, B is quant profile, C is p50/p95/p99 latencies, D is cost$/1k tokens, E is compatibility notes. For the pilot we recommended pinning route "payments-verify" to rwd-13b-8k and background reconciliation to rwd-7b-q4f.
[06:33] Marcus Allen: can we set soft-shadow first to validate outputs for 24 hours before hard pin?
[06:38] Priya Desai: absolutely — run shadow at 100% but route 0% until validated, or run partial shadow sampling 10% to start.
[06:46] Lea Torres: what about hallucination/regression monitoring across models? we need alerts if a model starts output regressions on critical prompts.
[06:55] Priya Desai: Redwood Optimize can run evals against your golden prompt set and raise alerts if quality drifts beyond thresholds. we recommend an eval suite for the pilot.

-- Objections and cost tradeoffs --
[07:12] Marcus Allen: finance will push back on keeping dedicated pool large enough for worst-case failover. how costly is warm standby vs small burstable?
[07:22] Jordan Kim: warm standby is more predictable but costlier. we can propose a hybrid: smaller dedicated baseline plus scheduled burst windows and a policy that only fails to hosted if authorised. we'll run a cost simulation with your workload traces.
[07:36] Marcus Allen: ok please include a 6 month cost delta with 3 scenarios.

[07:44] Tom Wu: during a cutover we want a playbook step to notify downstream systems and freeze refunds for a 2 minute window to avoid dup ops — can you include webhook hooks in the runbook?
[07:55] Priya Desai: yes we can include a webhook post and pre-hook to the cutover flow so your systems can respond.

-- Small misunderstandings / transcription quirks --
[08:10] Jordan Kim: (note) when I said KMS I may have mumbled AWS KMS, Redwood supports both AWS KMS and customer HSMs via standard interface.
[08:20] Lea Torres: (laughing) sorry I thought you said "KMS is magic system" earlier in notes.

-- Final recap and explicit next steps --
[08:30] Jordan Kim: recap: 1) Priya to run dedicated emergency cutover sim, capture token-level metrics and warmup times; 2) Nova to share traces and network constraints; 3) Jordan to share SOC2/KMS docs and the pricing sheet; 4) schedule dry-run with SREs week of 8/24. agree?
[08:50] Marcus Allen: agreed. we want the dry-run to include a simulated outage and a full rollback scenario.
[08:58] Tom Wu: include a step to validate cache reuse across variants, that's critical.
[09:04] Priya Desai: will do — I'll include cache warmup histograms in the sim report.
[09:12] Jordan Kim: any blockers on timeline?
[09:16] Lea Torres: legal needs the KMS/HSM diagram before we approve cross-region failover, that's the only gating item.
[09:24] Jordan Kim: we'll prioritize that doc and get it today.

[09:30] Jordan Kim: ok we'll wrap — thanks everyone, look out for the follow-ups in the next 48 hours.
[09:37] Marcus Allen: thanks.
[09:40] Lea Torres: thanks all.

Notes: some timestamps after 09:40 are system marker noise; full raw transcript in shared drive.
